neighbours.label: In English, the word ' so' when it opens a purpose clause right after an action and its object, with no comma before it ('hid the key so they couldn't find it', 'so that we could'); it fires on 'so' itself, so a degree 'so' straight after a verb and its object ('fixed it so quickly') can also fire. Quiet for ', so' after a comma, 'and so', 'so on', sentence-initial 'So', degree 'so' after is/was/felt, 'I think so', and for purpose said without 'so' ('in order to', 'lest', 'because').
neighbours.short: purpose 'so' right after an action, no comma
fire: She hid the key under the mat so the kids couldn't find it.
We moved the meeting to Friday so that everyone could attend.
He left the porch light on so his sister would see the house.
Please print the report so we can review it tonight.
They painted the fence green so it would blend with the hedge.
I wrapped the vase in newspaper so it wouldn't break in the van.
The coach changed the lineup so that the younger players got more time.
Turn the volume down so the baby can sleep.
quiet: She hid the key under the mat, so the kids couldn't find it.
We moved the meeting to Friday in order to let everyone attend.
He left the porch light on because his sister was coming home late.
So we printed the report and reviewed it tonight.
They painted the fence green, and so it blended with the hedge.
I wrapped the vase in newspaper lest it break in the van.
The coach said the younger players need more time, and I think so too.
The baby was so tired that she fell asleep at once.

predictions: 8/8 fire above 0.20, no near miss at 0.30 (comma-so twin is the riskiest)
